newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan cancels 25,000T corn shipment over epidemic.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan cancels 25,000T corn shipment over epidemic.

text.p: Taiwan's Bergerco, an affiliate of U.S. supplier Peavey, cancelled delivery of a 25,000-tonne shipment of U.S. corn due to the island's hog crisis, which has slashed local demand for feed, traders said on Friday.
The parcel shipment was bought through a private negotiation on behalf of some smaller Taiwan feed producers and had been slated for delivery in May, traders said.
Further details of the shipment were not available.
Traders attributed the cancellation to Taiwan's ongoing hog industry hog foot and mouth disease crisis.

Taiwan banned all pork exports on March 20, the day the disease was confirmed on nine breeding centres. As of Friday, the epidemic had spread to more than 800 feedlots despite an army-led eradication campaign to slaughter all pigs, healthy or otherwise, at all affected farms.
The crisis has battered the stock market, threatened to slow the island's gathering economic recovery and promised thousands of layoffs in the huge feedlot and meat-packing sector.
Experts believe more than one million hogs will have to be destroyed, while millions more were being vaccinated against the deadly contagion.
Taiwan corn buyers have estimated the crisis would slash the island's feed corn imports by about one-fifth.

A Reuters survey of five major grain importers found that all expected significant reductions in corn imports, with most estimating the downturn at about 1.2 million tonnes of the island's annual imports of 6.5 million tonnes.
Since March 20, Taiwan importers have cancelled tenders for nearly 200,000 tonnes of corn and soybeans due chiefly to plunging demand for feed.
